newsitem.title: USA: Cornerstone in $1.06 bln property deal - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Cornerstone in $1.06 bln property deal - WSJ.

text.p: Cornerstone Properties Inc has agreed to buy 11 properties in six U.S. cities from a Dutch pension fund for $1.06 billion in stock and cash, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday.
The company is expected to announce the deal as early as today, the paper said in its electronic edition.

Under the terms of the deal, Cornerstone will pay $508 million in cash and $547 million in stock to the Atlanta-based Dutch Institutional Holding Co -- part of one of the Netherlands' biggest pension funds.
The fund will also loan Cornerstone $250 million, to be repaid over ten years, the paper said.
The portfolio includes two buildings in Atlanta, three in Alexandria, Virginia, two in Boston, two in Washington, one in Charlotte, N.C., and one in Chicago, the paper said.
After the deal, Dutch Institutional will hold about 40.0 percent of Cornerstone's stock and take two seats on Cornerstone's 12-member board, the paper added.
